sources.title: RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4-BF16-LMHead · Hugging Face
sources.snippet: The RadixArk Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4-BF16-LMHead model is a variant of RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4, the quantized version of Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B produced at RadixArk using NVIDIA Model Optimizer with a mixed NVFP4 W4A4 recipe.

sources.title: RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 · Hugging Face
sources.snippet: Third-Party Community Consideration This model is not owned or developed by RadixArk. It is a quantized derivative of Qwen's model; see the upstream Qwen3.8-27B model card for the source model's capabilities, training information, limitations, and license.

sources.title: Qwen3.8 27B on SGLang for RTX PRO 6000 - GitHub
sources.snippet: Existing clones (git pull): the default Hub id changed to RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4-BF16-LMHead. Hugging Face caches per repo, so the old packed-FP4 tree is not reused — the next start downloads ~24 GB into a new folder and leaves ~22 GB unused unless you delete it:

sources.title: Qwen3.8 27B on SGLang for DGX Spark - GitHub
sources.snippet: Qwen3.8 27B on SGLang for DGX Spark by Mia's AI Lab Opinionated, ready-to-run scripts to serve Qwen3.8-27B with SGLang in Docker on an NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, aarch64). Three swap-in serving modes — EAGLE/MTP, DSpark, or DFlash2 — with every tuning choice measured on-device instead of guessed. DSpark and DFlash2 are faster on code.

sources.title: Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 on a single DGX Spark - NVIDIA Developer Forums
sources.snippet: Qwen3.8-27B was released today, and unsloth put up an NVFP4 quantization the same afternoon. It runs on a single DGX Spark without any modification to vLLM. This is what I found getting it up, including a packaging bug in the checkpoint that silently truncates every prompt at 2048 tokens. EDIT: Unsloth meanwhile uploaded a fixed version, so you can ignore the section about the tokenizer bug ...
